seo.title: Google Business Profile Services: How to Add
seo.meta_description: How to add services to your Google Business Profile for Anaheim and Orange County businesses: suggested and custom services, prices, descriptions and rules.

h1: Google Business Profile Services: List Everything You Offer
answer: Google Business Profile services let service businesses list what they offer, with descriptions and prices, directly on their profile. Google says a service may be highlighted when local customers search for it, and people can see your full list under Services in Google Maps. Anaheim and Orange County businesses should add suggested services, create custom ones where needed and follow Google's naming rules.
key_takeaways: Services can be highlighted for matching searches.
Custom names must follow Google's rules.

sections.heading: What the services list does
sections.body_html: Google's help page says businesses in certain categories, like service businesses, can showcase their offerings on their profile. When local customers search for something you provide, that service may be highlighted, and in the Google Maps app customers can view your full menu under Services.

sections.heading: Suggested services
sections.body_html: Google offers suggested services tailored to your business type. Its example: a plumbing business might see options such as Install faucet or Repair toilet. Start by selecting every suggestion that matches what you really do.

sections.heading: Custom services
sections.body_html: If a service is not listed, you can add a custom service. Google warns that custom services that violate policy are rejected automatically, and says to avoid profanity, gibberish, personal information, prices or phone numbers in custom service names.

sections.heading: How to add services
sections.body_html: Go to your Business Profile, select Edit services, choose the services you want and save. To add more, select Edit services, then Add more services, or Add custom service if yours is not listed.

sections.heading: Add descriptions and prices
sections.body_html: Select a service under Edit services to add a price and a description. Keep prices in the price field, not in the service name, and write descriptions that say what is included.

sections.heading: Group services into categories
sections.body_html: Under Edit services, select Add a new business category to group services. This keeps a long list easy to read, for example separating repairs from installations.

sections.heading: Match services to your website
sections.body_html: Use the same names for services on your profile and on your website's service pages. Consistent naming helps Google and AI assistants connect searches to the right page.

sections.heading: Services and categories work together
sections.body_html: Your categories set the broad relevance; services add detail. If a service you offer has its own category in Google's list, consider adding it as an additional category as well.

sections.heading: Keep the list current
sections.body_html: Remove services you stop offering and add new ones when you launch them. An out-of-date list leads to calls you cannot help with.

sections.heading: Services for service-area businesses
sections.body_html: For trades that visit customers, a complete services list combined with a correct service area tells Google both what you do and where you do it.

sections.heading: Checklist
sections.body_html:
• All matching suggested services selected.
  • Custom services added for the rest.
  • No prices or phone numbers in names.
  • Descriptions written.
  • Prices added where useful.
  • Services grouped into categories.
  • Names match website service pages.

sections.heading: Common services mistakes
sections.body_html:
• Relying only on the primary category and leaving the services list empty.
  • Putting prices, phone numbers or city names into custom service names.
  • Listing services the business no longer offers, which leads to wasted calls.
  • Using different names for the same service on the profile and the website.
  • Writing no descriptions, so customers cannot tell what each service includes.

sections.heading: How to decide what to list
sections.body_html: Start from what customers actually ask for, not from internal job codes. Look at the last few months of calls, emails and invoices and note the words customers use: they may say water heater replacement where your team says tank install. Use the customer's words for service names and descriptions. Then rank services by how much they matter to the business and make sure the most valuable ones have clear descriptions and, where it helps, a price or price range. Review the list whenever you add or drop a service. For trades and service businesses across Anaheim and Orange County, a complete, plain-language services list is one of the simplest ways to show up for the specific jobs you want more of.

sections.heading: An example
sections.body_html: Imagine an electrician in Anaheim whose profile lists only the category Electrician. The owner opens Edit services, selects suggested services such as panel upgrades and lighting installation, adds a custom service for EV charger installation, writes a short description and price range for each, and groups them into installations and repairs. The website's service pages use the same names.

sections.heading: How this fits your local plan
sections.body_html: It helps to see where this sits in the bigger picture. Google ranks local results mainly on relevance, distance and popularity, and AI assistants lean on the same public information: your Business Profile, your website, other listings and what customers write. For a business in Anaheim or anywhere in Orange County, the most reliable plan is simple and repeated: keep every listing accurate, explain each service clearly on its own page, show real proof of your work and reply to customers. Small improvements here compound, and they are far harder for competitors to copy than an ad budget.

sections.heading: Questions owners ask us
sections.body_html: Owners often ask how many services to list. List every service you genuinely want enquiries for, grouped so the list stays easy to scan; there is no prize for padding it with services you rarely do. Another common question is whether prices must be shown. Prices are optional, but a price or range can filter out poor-fit enquiries and build trust. Owners also ask whether services replace service pages on the website. They do not: the profile list helps people on Google, while a dedicated page for each important service gives Google and AI assistants the detail they need. A good rule of thumb is that every service worth listing on the profile is worth a short page of its own, with the same name, a plain description of what is included, the areas you cover and how to get a quote. Link that page from your services list where Google allows, and from your homepage, so customers and search engines can find it easily.

sections.heading: What to do this week
sections.body_html:
1. Open Edit services.
  2. Select every matching suggestion.
  3. Add custom services and descriptions.
  4. Match names on your website.

sections.heading: When to get help
sections.body_html: Plenty of owners handle this themselves. Outside help pays off when time is short, when the business has many locations or when a problem is costing calls every day it stays unresolved. Be wary of anyone who promises guaranteed positions or asks for your verification codes or passwords; Google says nobody can pay for a better local ranking. Look for clear explanations, honest timelines and reporting tied to real enquiries. Chimera offers exactly that to businesses in Anaheim and across Orange County.

sections.heading: The short version
sections.body_html: Select every matching suggested service, add custom ones within Google's rules, include descriptions and prices, group them and match your website. Chimera, based in Anaheim, builds complete service lists for Orange County businesses.

faqs.q: How do I add services to my Google Business Profile?
faqs.a: Select Edit services, choose services or add custom ones, then save.

faqs.q: Do services help my business show up in search?
faqs.a: Google says a service may be highlighted when local customers search for it.

faqs.q: Can I add prices to services?
faqs.a: Yes, in the price field for each service.

faqs.q: Why was my custom service rejected?
faqs.a: Custom names with profanity, gibberish, personal information, prices or phone numbers are rejected.

faqs.q: Where do customers see my services?
faqs.a: On your profile, and under Services in the Google Maps app.

faqs.q: Should service names match my website?
faqs.a: Yes. Consistent names help Google and AI assistants.
